# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.10 on Mon Aug 31 09:00:00 2026
# The two-line -m recent recipe, copied one line at a time — and each half
# lost its partner. ssh kept only the READER: the DROP consults list SSH
# that nothing ever fills, so the "brute-force protection" is constant-false
# and every attempt sails to the ACCEPT below. wireguard kept only the
# WRITER: list WG fills forever while nothing consults it. Both load
# without a word, and the ruleset reads like it throttles.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --update --seconds 60 --hitcount 4 --name SSH -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p udp --dport 51820 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --set --name WG
-A INPUT -p udp --dport 51820 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m limit --limit 5/min -j LOG --log-prefix "input-drop: "
COMMIT
